definitions.explanation: Bleeding from the nose. A common minor condition, especially in children.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{鼻血|はなぢ}を{出|だ}したので、ティッシュを{渡|わた}した。
examples.english: The child got a nosebleed, so I gave them a tissue.

examples.japanese: {乾燥|かんそう}した{季節|きせつ}は{鼻血|はなぢ}が{出|で}やすいので、{加湿器|かしつき}を{使|つか}うとよい。
examples.english: Nosebleeds happen more easily in the dry season, so it's good to use a humidifier.

notes:
USAGE:
The most common pattern is {鼻血|はなぢ}が{出|で}る (to get a nosebleed, literally "a nosebleed comes out"). The transitive form {鼻血|はなぢ}を{出|だ}す (to produce a nosebleed) is used when describing someone else's nosebleed or an action causing one.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鼻血|はなぢ}が{出|で}る (to have a nosebleed)
- {鼻血|はなぢ}を{出|だ}す (to get/cause a nosebleed)
- {鼻血|はなぢ}が{止|と}まらない (the nosebleed won't stop)
- {鼻血|はなぢ}を{拭|ふ}く (to wipe a nosebleed)

SPELLING NOTE:
The reading is はなぢ (with ぢ), not はなじ. This is because the second element is {血|ち} (blood), which becomes voiced (ぢ) in compound words through rendaku.
